newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares close up ahead of Chidambaram speech.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares close up ahead of Chidambaram speech.

text.p: Indian blue chips ended higher on Monday driven by hopes Indian Finance Minister Chidambaram would offer incentives to retail and institutional investors, traders said.
Chidambaram's reply to a debate on the federal budget for 1996/97 (April-March) is scheduled for Tuesday. He plans to make a more detailed reply to the finance bill on September 9 or 10.
The finance minister assured institutional investors at a recent meeting some changes in the budget proposals would be implemented fairly quickly, market sources said.
Some analysts expect a dilution in the controversial 12.9 percent minimum alternate tax (MAT) announced in the budget.
"Export earnings may be exempt from MAT," one analyst said.
But an institutional investor present at the meeting with Chidambaram said it was unlikely he would change tax proposals.
"There may not be anything drastic on the tax front but he is likely to announce some sops for investors," he said.
The speech -- originally scheduled for Monday -- was postponed when the lower house of the Indian parliament was adjourned without transacting any business on Monday due to the death of a member.
In Delhi, the index closed 4.66 points higher at 807.59 ahead of the finance minister's speech.
"Encouraging first quarter performance by some companies aided the market," said Shree Bhagwan at brokers Means Leasing.
The Calcutta stocks index ended 5.58 points higher at 456.16, supported by bids from foreign investors.

"The renewed buying interest in shares of medium cap firms is a good sign. Blue chips also moved up but profit-taking at higher levels erased gains," said Aprajit Sharma of brokers Jet Age Securities.
